To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rats form distinct memorial representations of different unconditioned stimuli that can be selectively activated by the appropriate conditioned stimuli and that these selective responses can be modulated by systemic and intracerebro-ventricular injections of metabolic antimetabolites.
the activation of "metaborepresents" of USs is selectively promoted by signals that indicate the unavailability of the nutrients that are associated with the USs in the training environment.
the activation of the memory representations of different USs is selectively promoted by lipoprivic and/or glucoprivic treatments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hypothesis that the activation of the representations of USs is a function of the metabolic status of the organism.
the hypothesis that the activation of the representations of USs is determined by the metabolic status of the organism at the time of CS-US pairings and by the metabolic state at the time of testing.
a new class of memories that are activated by metabolic signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this series of studies demonstrate that rats can form and selectively activate representations (or "memories") of the metabolic properties of USs.
these findings show that metabolic signals are capable of selectively activating the representations of the metabolic consequences of food intake.
metabolic signals are involved in the selective activation of memories of USs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain encodes and selectively activates distinct memorial representations for different USs.
the metabolic status of the body is encoded in the brain, and that this encoding can be selectively activated by appropriate metabolic manipulations.
metabolic memories," like other forms of associative learning, can be selectively activated by the appropriate metabolic signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rats encode and activate "metabolic memories," which may be important in the regulation of ingestive behavior.
the activation of the "metabolic memories", which are the representations of USs, can be modulated by the availability of nutrients in the body.
the activation of the "metabolic memories of food" is a dynamic process that is regulated in part by the metabolic status of the body and the afferent input from the viscera.
